idea.body: A straight line through a point is really just an angle laid out flat, measuring 180 degrees. Any angle can be split exactly in half by a ray called its bisector. A drone's camera gimbal opened to 70 degrees is split by its centerline into two 35 degree halves. Two angles that share a vertex and a ray, together lying along a straight line, are a linear pair. A linear pair always adds to 180 degrees. Two angles made by two crossing lines, sitting directly across the vertex from each other, are vertical angles, and vertical angles are always equal. Points on a line work like a number line too. When a point sits between two others, the two short distances between them add up to the long one.

figure.alt: A straight line split by a ray into two angles, 118 degrees and an unknown angle.

workedExample.prompt: A radio mast is held by a guy wire that meets the flat ground. The wire and the mast form two adjacent angles that together lie along the ground: a linear pair. One of the two angles measures 118 degrees. Find the other angle.
steps: The two angles share a vertex and a ray, and together they lie along the flat ground, so they are a linear pair.
A linear pair always adds up to 180 degrees.
Subtract the known angle from 180: 180 - 118 = 62.
The other angle measures 62 degrees.

figure.alt: A guy wire meeting flat ground, forming a linear pair of 118 degrees and an unknown angle.

ways.name: The linear pair adds to 180
ways.when: Use this any time two adjacent angles together lie along a straight line.
steps: A solar panel brace meets flat ground, forming a linear pair of angles.
One angle measures 132 degrees.
A linear pair always adds up to 180 degrees.
Subtract the known angle from 180: 180 minus 132 is 48.
The other angle measures 48 degrees.
ways.example: A solar panel brace meets the ground, forming a linear pair. One angle is 132 degrees. Find the other.
ways.trap: Subtracting from 90 instead of 180, confusing a linear pair with complementary angles.

ways.name: Vertical angles are equal
ways.when: Use this when two straight wires or beams cross, making angles directly across from each other.
steps: Two guy wires cross at a point, making four angles around it.
One angle measures 76 degrees.
The angle directly across from it, the vertical angle, is always equal.
No arithmetic needed: the other angle also measures 76 degrees.
ways.example: Two wires cross, making vertical angles. One measures 76 degrees. Find the angle directly across from it.
ways.trap: Matching it to the angle right next to it instead of the one straight across the vertex.

ways.name: Split the angle in half
ways.when: Use this when a ray bisects an angle and you need the measure of each half.
steps: A camera gimbal opens to 84 degrees.
A support strut bisects the opening exactly in half.
A bisector always splits an angle into two equal halves.
Divide by 2: 84 divided by 2 is 42.
Each half measures 42 degrees.
ways.example: A gimbal opens to 84 degrees. A strut bisects it exactly in half. Find each half.
ways.trap: Forgetting to divide by 2 and giving the whole angle as the answer for each half.

ways.name: Add distances along a line
ways.when: Use this when one point sits between two others on the same straight path.
steps: A rover's path has points A, B and C in a straight line, with B between A and C.
AB measures 14 meters and BC measures 9 meters.
When B is between A and C, AB plus BC equals AC.
Add the two distances: 14 plus 9 is 23.
AC measures 23 meters.
ways.example: Point B sits between A and C on a straight path. AB is 14 meters and BC is 9 meters. Find AC.
ways.trap: Subtracting the two distances instead of adding them, since B lies between rather than outside.

stretch.prompt: A clock reads 3:40. Find the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees.
explanation: The minute hand sits at 6 degrees times the minutes, measured from 12.
At 40 minutes, the minute hand is at 6 x 40 = 240 degrees.
The hour hand sits at 30 degrees times the hour, plus half a degree per minute past the hour.
At 3:40, the hour hand is at 30 x 3 + 0.5 x 40 = 110 degrees.
The difference is 130 degrees, and that is already the smaller angle.
